recipes.name: Sweet Noodle Kugel
recipes.summary: A Jewish holiday favorite: egg noodles baked in a sweet, creamy custard of cottage cheese, sour cream and cream cheese with a cinnamon top.

ingredients.prep: melted, plus more for the dish

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and butter the baking dish. Cook the noodles in boiling salted water 2 minutes less than the package time. Drain.
In a large bowl, whisk the cream cheese, butter and sugar until smooth. Whisk in the eggs one at a time, then the cottage cheese, sour cream, milk, vanilla and salt.
Fold in the noodles and raisins. Spread in the dish. Mix the topping sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over.
Bake 55 to 60 minutes, until set in the center, golden on top and 160°F inside. Cool 15 minutes before cutting.
recipes.make_ahead: Bake up to 2 days ahead. Serve warm, at room temperature or cold. Reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze baked squares wrapped well for up to 2 months.

leftovers.text: Eat a cold square for breakfast with fruit.

recipes.kids: Kids can stir in the noodles and sprinkle the cinnamon sugar.

recipes.name: Hot Spinach Artichoke Dip
recipes.summary: A bubbly, cheesy dip of spinach, artichoke hearts, cream cheese, sour cream, mozzarella and Parmesan.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Stir the cream cheese, sour cream, mayonnaise, garlic, pepper and pepper flakes until smooth. Fold in the spinach, artichokes, 3/4 cup mozzarella and the Parmesan.
Spread in the baking dish and top with the remaining mozzarella.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbling at the edges and lightly browned. Serve hot with chips, crackers or vegetables.
recipes.make_ahead: Assemble up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate; add 5 to 10 minutes to the baking time.

leftovers.text: Spread leftovers on a tortilla, add chicken and fold it into a quesadilla. Reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Serve with soft pita wedges or bell pepper strips.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve with vegetables or corn chips.

recipes.name: Crustless Spinach and Feta Pie
recipes.summary: The flavors of Greek spanakopita (spinach, feta, dill and green onions) baked in an easy egg and cottage cheese custard with no crust.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and oil the pie dish.
Whisk the eggs in a large bowl. Stir in the cottage cheese, feta, green onions, dill, parsley, Parmesan, pepper and nutmeg, then the spinach. (Feta is salty, so no salt is added.)
Spread in the dish. Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until puffed, golden at the edges and set in the center (160°F). Cool 10 minutes before slicing.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Eat cold or reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze wedges for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Pack a cold wedge for lunch with a piece of fruit.

recipes.kids: Kids can help squeeze the spinach dry in a towel; it is fun and it matters.

prep_day.ahead: Bake the pie for breakfasts and lunches.

recipes.name: Cottage Cheese Pancakes
recipes.summary: Tender, high-protein pancakes made with cottage cheese and eggs. Blend the batter smooth or leave it a little lumpy.
steps: Blend or whisk the cottage cheese, eggs, milk, sugar and vanilla. Stir in the flour, baking powder and salt just until mixed.

Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat and brush with butter. Pour scant 1/4 cups of batter. Cook 2 to 3 minutes, until the bottoms are golden and the edges look set, then flip and cook 2 minutes more, until cooked through.
Serve with fruit and syrup.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat in the toaster or microwave.

freezer.text: Freeze in one layer, then bag, for up to 2 months.

leftovers.text: Spread a cold pancake with jam for a snack.

recipes.kids: These are softer than regular pancakes; keep them small so they are easy to flip.

recipes.name: Lazy Pierogi (Cottage Cheese Dumplings)
recipes.summary: A Polish family favorite: soft dumplings of cottage cheese, egg and flour, boiled and tossed with butter. Serve them sweet with cinnamon sugar or savory with onions.
steps: Mash the cottage cheese with a fork until the curds are small. Stir in the eggs, salt and sugar, then the flour, until a soft, sticky dough forms.
Divide the dough in 4. On a well-floured counter, roll each piece into a rope about 1 inch thick, then press it slightly flat and cut on an angle into 1-inch pieces.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the dumplings in 2 batches: once they float, cook 2 minutes more, until puffed and cooked through. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Toss with melted butter and sprinkle with the cinnamon and sugar. Serve with sour cream if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Cooked dumplings keep 3 days in the fridge; brown them in butter in a skillet to reheat.

freezer.text: Freeze uncooked dumplings on a floured tray, then bag, for up to 2 months. Boil from frozen, adding 2 minutes.

leftovers.text: Brown leftover dumplings in butter for a crisp breakfast.

recipes.kids: Kids can roll the ropes and cut the dumplings with a butter knife.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend; the dough will be softer.

recipes.name: Creamy Cottage Cheese Dill Dip
recipes.summary: Cottage cheese blended smooth with fresh dill, chives and lemon. A high-protein dip for vegetables and crackers.
steps: Blend the cottage cheese and lemon juice until smooth and creamy, about 1 minute.
Add the dill, chives, garlic, salt and pepper and pulse a few times.
Chill 30 minutes so the flavors blend. Serve with vegetables or crackers.

leftovers.text: Spread it on a bagel or use it as a sandwich spread.

recipes.kids: Serve with cucumber rounds, snap peas and carrot sticks.

prep_day.ahead: Make the dip and cut vegetables for snack boxes.

recipes.name: Spinach Lasagna Roll-Ups
recipes.summary: Lasagna noodles rolled around a ricotta, spinach and basil filling and baked in marinara under melted mozzarella. Easy to portion.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook the noodles in boiling salted water by the package directions. Drain and lay flat on oiled foil so they do not stick.
Mix the ricotta, spinach, egg, Parmesan, basil, garlic, salt and pepper.
Spread 1 cup marinara in the baking dish. Spread about 3 tablespoons filling along each noodle and roll it up. Set them seam side down in the dish.
Spoon the rest of the sauce over and sprinkle with mozzarella. Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes. Uncover and bake 10 minutes more, until bubbling and 165°F in the center.
recipes.make_ahead: Assemble up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate; add 10 minutes to the covered time.

freezer.text: Freeze unbaked roll-ups in a foil pan, well wrapped, for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge and bake as directed.

leftovers.text: Reheat 2 roll-ups covered in the microwave to 165°F for lunch.

recipes.kids: Kids can spread the filling and roll the noodles.

prep_day.ahead: Assemble the roll-ups and refrigerate or freeze.

recipes.name: Lemon Ricotta Pancakes
recipes.summary: Light, moist pancakes with ricotta and fresh lemon zest. Special enough for a weekend, easy enough for a weekday.

ingredients.prep: melted, plus more for the pan

steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl whisk the ricotta, milk, eggs, melted butter, lemon zest, lemon juice and vanilla. Fold into the dry ingredients just until mixed; the batter will be thick.
Heat a griddle over medium heat and brush with butter. Cook 1/4-cup scoops 2 to 3 minutes, until golden underneath and set at the edges. Flip and cook 2 minutes more.
recipes.make_ahead: Mix the dry ingredients the night before.

freezer.text: Freeze cooled pancakes in one layer, then bag, for up to 2 months. Reheat in the toaster.

leftovers.text: Warm leftover pancakes in the toaster for a fast school-day breakfast.

recipes.kids: Kids can zest the lemon with a grown-up and whisk the batter.

recipes.name: Spinach and Ricotta Calzones
recipes.summary: Store-bought pizza dough folded around ricotta, mozzarella, spinach and Parmesan, baked golden and served with marinara for dipping.
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F and line the baking sheets with parchment. Mix the ricotta, mozzarella, Parmesan, spinach, garlic and Italian seasoning.
Cut the dough into 4 pieces. On a floured counter, roll each into an 8-inch circle.
Spoon a quarter of the filling onto half of each circle, leaving a 1-inch border. Fold over, press the edges and crimp with a fork. Cut 2 small slits in the top and brush with oil.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes, until deep golden. Cool 5 minutes (the filling is very hot) and serve with marinara.
recipes.make_ahead: Assemble up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerate on the pan.

freezer.text: Freeze baked calzones for up to 2 months. Reheat in a 375°F oven about 20 minutes, to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Pack a cold calzone for lunch, or reheat it to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can roll the dough and add their own fillings, such as pepperoni or chopped vegetables.

prep_day.ahead: Bake and freeze a batch for lunches.

recipes.name: Broccoli Alfredo Penne
recipes.summary: Penne and broccoli in a homemade Alfredo sauce of cream, butter, garlic and Parmesan. Add leftover chicken if you like.
steps: Cook the penne in a large pot of boiling salted water by the package directions. Add the broccoli for the last 3 minutes. Save 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic for 1 minute. Add the cream and simmer gently 4 to 5 minutes, until slightly thick.
Lower the heat and whisk in the Parmesan a handful at a time until smooth. Add the salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Toss the pasta, broccoli and chicken in the sauce, adding pasta water a splash at a time until creamy. If using chicken, heat until it reaches 165°F.
recipes.make_ahead: Best fresh; cream sauces thicken in the fridge. Leftovers keep 3 days.

leftovers.text: Reheat with a splash of milk, stirring, to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids who like mac and cheese usually love this.

recipes.name: Classic Cream Scones
recipes.summary: Tender, lightly sweet scones made with heavy cream. Add dried fruit or chocolate chips if you like.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. Rub in the butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs with a few pea-size pieces.
Stir in the cream, vanilla and dried fruit with a fork just until a shaggy dough forms. Turn out and gently pat into an 8-inch circle about 3/4 inch thick.
Cut into 8 wedges, set them on the sheet and brush with cream. Bake 15 to 18 minutes, until golden. Cool 10 minutes.
recipes.make_ahead: Shape and cut the scones, then refrigerate overnight on the pan; bake in the morning.

freezer.text: Freeze unbaked wedges on a tray, then bag, for up to 2 months. Bake from frozen, adding 3 to 5 minutes.

leftovers.text: Warm a day-old scone in a 300°F oven for 5 minutes.

recipes.kids: Kids can pat out the dough and press in the fruit.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend with xanthan gum.

recipes.name: Flaky Buttermilk Biscuits
recipes.summary: Tall, tender Southern-style biscuits from flour, cold butter and buttermilk. Fold the dough a few times for flaky layers.
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F. Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and sugar in a large bowl.
Cut in the cold butter until it is the size of peas. Stir in the buttermilk with a fork just until the dough comes together.
Turn out onto a floured counter and pat into a rectangle. Fold it in thirds like a letter, pat it out again and repeat twice. Pat to 3/4 inch thick.
Cut biscuits straight down without twisting and set them touching on the baking sheet. Re-pat the scraps once. Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until golden. Brush with melted butter.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the biscuits and freeze them unbaked.

freezer.text: Freeze unbaked biscuits on a tray, then bag, for up to 2 months. Bake from frozen at 425°F for 18 to 22 minutes.

leftovers.text: Split a leftover biscuit, toast it and top with an egg and cheese.

recipes.kids: Kids can cut the biscuits. Press straight down for tall ones.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend made for biscuits.

recipes.name: Mini Cheesecakes
recipes.summary: Little cheesecakes with a graham cracker crust baked in a muffin tin. Top them with fresh berries.
steps: Heat the oven to 325°F and line a muffin tin with paper liners. Mix the cracker crumbs, butter and sugar and press about 1 tablespoon into each liner.
Beat the cream cheese and sugar until smooth. Beat in the eggs one at a time on low, then the sour cream, vanilla and lemon juice. Do not overbeat.
Divide the filling among the cups. Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until the edges are set and the centers just jiggle (they reach 160°F).
Cool in the pan 30 minutes, then refrigerate at least 2 hours. Top with berries.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge, covered.

freezer.text: Freeze without the fruit for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge.

recipes.kids: Kids can press the crust into the liners and add the berries.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free graham crackers or skip the crust.

prep_day.ahead: Bake a day ahead for a party.
